== con-leche/ConLeche/MainTheorem.lean#L90-L117
    90  /-- **The main theorem.**  Every environment the checker accepts has a
    91  model in every set theory — at every `Nat.div`/`Nat.mod` pin list, so
    92  consistency does not depend on which variants the install gate is
    93  handed (the empty list included: under it every stream that declares
    94  `Nat.div` declines).  The shipped binary runs the fold at
    95  `natOpPinSets`. -/
    96  theorem model_exists (V : Type w) [SetTheory V]
    97      (pins : List NatOpPinSet) (ds : Array Declaration) (env : Env)
    98      (accepted : checkDecls .verified pins ds = .ok env) :
    99      Nonempty (Model V env) := by
   100    obtain ⟨m⟩ := Cached.checkDecls_sound (V := V) rfl accepted
   101    exact ⟨Model.Model.ofEnvModelM m⟩
   102  
   103  open Frontend in
   104  /-- **The main corollary.**  A file declaring a theorem of type `False`
   105  in the shape `jsonWithTheoremFalse` describes is rejected: the parse
   106  reads the template's four lines into a theorem record of type `False`,
   107  the preparation keeps the record, and a stream holding it is never
   108  accepted.  At every pin list, as the main theorem: the shipped binary
   109  runs the fold at `natOpPinSets`. -/
   110  theorem no_False_declaration (V : Type w) [SetTheory V]
   111      (pins : List NatOpPinSet) (chunks : List ByteArray)
   112      (h : jsonWithTheoremFalse chunks) :
   113      ∃ e, (do
   114        let pre ← builtinPreludeE
   115        let r ← parseChunks chunks
   116        let ds := preparePrelude pre r.decls
   117        checkDecls .verified pins ds) = .error e := by

== crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs#L87-L202
    87  const USAGE: &str = "\
    88  usage: con-ron [--verified|--trusted] [--jobs=<n>] [--no-mark-persistent]
    89                 [--progress[=<stride>]] [--pins FILE|--no-pins]
    90                 FILE.ndjson
    91         con-ron --help
    92  
    93    (C), the Rust arena checker of con-ron's DESIGN.md section 8: con-leche's
    94    pure checker over an append-only DAG of per-constructor handle arrays, with
    95    con-leche's command line and con-leche's exit codes, so that
    96    scripts/diff-e2e.sh can run the same 383 fixtures against this binary and
    97    the Lean twin `con-ron-lean` alike.  A term is a u32 handle into a Vec: on
    98    the checking path there is no Arc, no tagged pointer and no reference count
    99    at all.  (The PINNED DATA the checker compares against is still
   100    con-leche's own constants as Expr values, interned into the persistent tier
   101    once at startup -- crates/con-ron-core/src/lib.rs says why.)
   102  
   103    --verified        the default, and the mode the main theorem is about: every
   104                      environment the fold accepts in this mode has a model in
   105                      every set theory (ConLeche.model_exists), so a stream
   106                      declaring a theorem of type False is never accepted.  What
   107                      the arena rewrite proves is that same statement about this
   108                      program's pipeline; the proof itself is phases P3 and P5
   109                      (DESIGN.md section 8.6) and is NOT done.
   110    --trusted         the unverified mode: the SAME checker bodies at the mode
   111                      with the certification-only work switched off.  An accept
   112                      in this mode is outside the theorem.
   113    --jobs=<n>        the check phase runs on <n> worker threads sharing the
   114                      persistent tier and the installed index by reference
   115                      (DESIGN.md section 8.3): each worker owns a scratch tier,
   116                      its own caches and a copy of the pin handles, and the
   117                      results are merged by record index and walked in record
   118                      order, so the verdict and the record a rejection names are
   119                      the same at every <n>.  Default: one per hardware thread,
   120                      capped at 16.  A worker reserves 1 GiB of stack, which a
   121                      `ulimit -v` must allow for.  0 or a non-numeral is a usage
   122                      error, as in con-leche.
   123    --no-mark-persistent
   124                      ACCEPTED AND A NO-OP, for a stronger reason than the
   125                      `con-ron` binary's: the mark it turns off is a
   126                      Lean-runtime reference-counting device
   127                      (Runtime.markPersistent), and this checker has no
   128                      reference counts at all -- a term is a u32 handle into a
   129                      Vec and the persistent tier is immutable in phase B.  A
   130                      run that passes it says so on stderr.
   131    --progress[=<stride>]
   132                      opt-in progress heartbeat on STDERR, one line shape per
   133                      phase:
   134                        con-ron: parse done: <N> fold records ... t=<s>s
   135                        con-ron: install <i>/<N> <decl> t=<s>s
   136                        con-ron: install done: <N>/<N> ..., <M> pending
   137                        con-ron: check <done>/<M> <kind> <name> t=<s>s
   138                        con-ron: check done: <M>/<M> t=<s>s
   139                        con-ron: done: parse <p>s, install <i>s, check <c>s
   140                      An install line is printed BEFORE every <stride>-th
   141                      declaration is installed, so a run that dies in the
   142                      install phase names the declaration it died in on its last
   143                      line; a check line is printed AFTER every <stride>-th
   144                      COMPLETED check.  On a failure the phase's closing line
   145                      says so and the summary still prints.  Bare --progress is
   146                      stride 1; a stride that is not a decimal numeral, or 0, is
   147                      a usage error.
   148    --pins FILE       con-ron's own, FOR TESTING: read the pin list from a
   149                      `con-ron-pins/1` dump instead of the core's own embedded
   150                      text (task #43), through the UNVERIFIED reader.  The pins
   151                      are interned into the persistent tier at startup, before
   152                      the fold (DESIGN.md section 8.6 P2d).
   153    --no-pins         con-ron's own, FOR TESTING: the empty pin list, the pin
   154                      loop's `[]` arm, under which a Nat.div/Nat.mod stream
   155                      declines.  Neither flag is needed for a normal run: the
   156                      pins are con-leche's `natOpPinSets`, embedded in the
   157                      verified core and decoded by it.
   158    --help            print this text on STDOUT and exit 0, in any argument
   159                      position; no input is read.  Its last line names the
   160                      global allocator THIS binary was built with (below), so a
   161                      measurement can be reproduced.
   162  
   163  build-time selection (cargo features, not command-line flags): the global
   164  allocator is `con-ron-dump`'s `#[global_allocator]`, chosen on this crate's
   165  dependency edge -- `cargo build --release` is mimalloc, `--no-default-features`
   166  is glibc `malloc`, and `--no-default-features --features jemalloc` is jemalloc.
   167  It is the same edge `crates/con-ron` has, so the two checkers are measured on
   168  the same allocator unless a build says otherwise.
   169  
   170  Any other option is a usage error: the run reports it, prints this text and
   171  exits 3 without reading its input.
   172  
   173  exit codes: 0 accepted, 1 rejected, 2 declined, 3 usage/malformed/internal.
   174  An out-of-memory condition is NEITHER: this program aborts the way Rust aborts
   175  on a failed allocation ('memory allocation of <n> bytes failed', SIGABRT,
   176  which a shell reports as 134).  A panic is exit 3.
   177  
   178  THE VERDICT LINE'S COUNT.  It counts the FILE's accepted declaration RECORDS:
   179  one per def/theorem/opaque/axiom/inductive/quot record the file declares.  The
   180  built-in prelude's own records are not counted, and neither are the records
   181  the in-process modeller generates; a stream record that declares a prelude
   182  declaration IS counted.  That count is a property of the INPUT; the number of
   183  environment CONSTANTS is not.
   184  
   185  THE BUILT-IN PRELUDE.  Every run installs, first and unconditionally, the
   186  checker's own little prelude -- the six pinned basis blocks (Eq, Nat, PUnit,
   187  Empty, False, Quot) and the toolchain's Bool and And blocks, embedded at build
   188  time -- so the pin-certified Nat operations find their ground whatever order
   189  the export chose.  It is parsed into the SAME store as the stream, which is
   190  what the persistent tier is for: the prelude's nodes and the stream's are
   191  hash-consed together.
   192  
   193  environment (con-leche's):
   194    CON_LECHE_INMODEL=0          turn the in-process modeller off; a mutual or
   195                                 nested block is then pushed bare and the FOLD
   196                                 declines it, having found no route
   197    CON_LECHE_INMODEL_CENSUS=1   report every mutual/nested block's outcome
   198                                 after the parse and stop (exit 2)
   199    CON_LECHE_PROJREC_TRACE      name each rewritten projection function
   200  These are the in-process modeller's debug switches and they go with it: no
   201  environment variable this program reads can shape a verdict, which is
   202  con-leche's own rule -- every such switch is a command-line flag.";

    19  //! |---|---|---|
    20  //! | 0 | `accepted N declarations` | every declaration checked; `N` counts the file's declaration records |

   499  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Expr.lean:286-404 Expr
   500  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Cached/ExprNodes.lean:113 mkApp
   501  /// `Expr.app`: hash tag 17; both ranges are the componentwise `max` and the
   502  /// level-param bit the disjunction.
   503  pub fn app(f: Expr, a: Expr) -> Expr {
   504      let df: u64 = data(&f);
   505      let da: u64 = data(&a);
   506      let h: u64 = hash32(name::mix_hash(
   507          17,
   508          name::mix_hash(hash_of_data(df), hash_of_data(da)),
   509      ));
   510      let d: u64 = pack_data(
   511          h,
   512          max_u64(bvar_of_data(df), bvar_of_data(da)),
   513          max_u64(fvar_of_data(df), fvar_of_data(da)),

  1328  pub fn decode(t: &[u8]) -> CheckM<Vec<NatOpPinSet>> {
  1329      let hdr = pins_header();
  1330      if !starts_with_from(t, &hdr, 0) {

  1332      } else {
  1333          run_records(t, hdr.len(), tables_new())

    19  //! | Rust | Lean twin | con-leche |
    20  //! |---|---|---|
    21  //! | `text` | none | none — the port's message rendering (`String` is `Vec<u32>`) |

    23  //! | `scan_types` | imported, not twinned | `ConLeche/Frontend/Scan/Types.lean` |
    24  //! | `scan_fast` | imported, not twinned | `ConLeche/Frontend/Scan/Fast.lean` (the `@[csimp]` twin the compiler *runs*; `Scan/Naive.lean` is the specification and is not ported) |

   639    | sort {u e} : LevelWF u → expr.sort u = ok e → ExprWF e
   640    | mk_const {n us e} : NameWF n → LevelsWF us → expr.mk_const n us = ok e → ExprWF e
   641    | app {f a e} : ExprWF f → ExprWF a → expr.app f a = ok e → ExprWF e
   642    | lam {ty b m e} : ExprWF ty → ExprWF b → BinderMetaWF m →
   643        expr.lam ty b m = ok e → ExprWF e
   644    | forall_e {ty b m e} : ExprWF ty → ExprWF b → BinderMetaWF m →
   645        expr.forall_e ty b m = ok e → ExprWF e
   646    | let_e {ty v b e} : ExprWF ty → ExprWF v → ExprWF b →
   647        expr.let_e ty v b = ok e → ExprWF e
   648    | lit {l e} : LiteralWF l → expr.lit l = ok e → ExprWF e

   895  theorem knot_induction {mode : env.CheckMode}
   896      (harms : ∀ fuel, Wrappers mode fuel → Bodies mode fuel) (fuel : Std.U64) :
   897      KnotSpec mode fuel := by
   898    have key : ∀ n : Nat, ∀ f : Std.U64, f.val = n → Wrappers mode f := by
   899      intro n
   900      induction n with
   901      | zero =>
   902        intro f hfv
   903        have h0 : f = 0#u64 := u64_val_inj (by rw [hfv]; rfl)
   904        subst h0; exact wrappers_zero mode
   905      | succ n ih =>
   906        intro f hfv
   907        have hlt : n < 2 ^ Std.UScalarTy.U64.numBits := by
   908          have h1 : f.val < 2 ^ Std.UScalarTy.U64.numBits := f.bv.isLt
   909          omega
   910        have hg : (Std.UScalar.ofNatCore n hlt : Std.U64).val = n :=

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L472-L490
   472  /// **The driver**: `checker::check_decls_phased` with the boundary visible —
   473  /// a straight line of calls into the verified crate, with the observer's
   474  /// lines between them and the pool in the place of phase B's sequential walk
   475  /// (task #97-P5-Driver):
   476  ///
   477  /// | step | here | in `check_decls_phased` |
   478  /// |---|---|---|
   479  /// | phase A | `checker::annot_fold_hooked(…, fold_start(), ds, 0, obs)` | the same call |
   480  /// | boundary | `checker::freeze_tier(&mut st.store)` | the same call |
   481  /// | phase B | `pool::check_pool(&tier, mode, &fe, &pend, &st.pins, workers, …)` | `checker::check_pending_worker(&tier, mode, &fe, &st.pins, &pend)` |
   482  /// | after | `checker::thaw_tier(&mut st.store, tier)` | the same call |
   483  ///
   484  /// Everything else here is the observer, which only ever holds `&` the state
   485  /// (the hook of phase A by the trait's own signature, the other lines through
   486  /// `&st.store`), so it cannot change an outcome.  So the capstone, which is
   487  /// stated about `check_decls_phased`, is about this function modulo the
   488  /// pool's one claim: its merged table, walked in record order, is what the
   489  /// verified one-worker walk `checker::check_pending_worker` returns
   490  /// (`pool.rs`'s note states it and what it rests on).

== crates/con-ron/src/pool.rs#L47-L105
    47  //! ## THE TRUSTED CLAIM, and the whole of it
    48  //!
    49  //! **`check_pool(pers, mode, fe, pend, pins, n, _)` returns what
    50  //! `checker::check_pending_worker(pers, mode, fe, pins, pend)` returns, at
    51  //! every worker count `n`** — the same verdict, and on a failure the same fold
    52  //! position.  `pool_is_check_pending_worker_at_every_jobs` is its test.  It
    53  //! rests on two arguments, and the second is the one master's pool did not
    54  //! need.
    55  //!
    56  //! **(1) Merge by record index — master's argument.**  A worker's result is
    57  //! the record's index with its outcome; the workers' arrays are merged *by
    58  //! record index* into one table and the table is walked in **record order**,
    59  //! stopping at the first failing record in fold order.  That walk is
    60  //! `check_pending_list`'s, whatever the workers' timing, so the pool cannot
    61  //! report the second failure of a stream that has two —
    62  //! `pool_reports_the_first_failure_at_every_jobs` is the test, at 1, 2, 3, 4
    63  //! and 8 workers on a list whose records 2 and 4 both fail.
    64  //!
    65  //! **The table is complete below the first failure**, which is what makes the
    66  //! walk total.  con-leche's argument, and the port's: a worker that fails
    67  //! record `f` lowers the shared `limit` to `f`, and a worker skips a claimed
    68  //! record at or above the limit.  Every value the limit ever holds is `m` or
    69  //! a *failing* index, hence at least the first failing index `f`; so a record
    70  //! below `f` is never skipped, and — the counter being monotone — it was
    71  //! claimed before `f` was and is finished by the worker that claimed it.
    72  //! Records above `f` may be missing from the table, and the walk never
    73  //! reaches them.  (A worker also never checks a record after its own first
    74  //! failure: every later claim is above it, hence at or above the limit.)
    75  //!
    76  //! Every access is `Relaxed`: a stale read of `limit` can only be *larger*
    77  //! than the current value, i.e. can only make a worker do work it could have
    78  //! skipped, and the results themselves travel through the `join` at the end
    79  //! of the scope, which is the release/acquire pair.
    80  //!
    81  //! **(2) A record's outcome does not depend on which records its worker
    82  //! checked before it — the deliberate difference from master.**  Master's
    83  //! pool checked every record from a fresh `cstate_new()`, so (1) was the
    84  //! whole argument.  Here a worker keeps ONE `AState` for the whole run, so
    85  //! record `k` is checked on a state its worker's earlier records have used —
    86  //! records `0..k` in the one-worker walk, some subsequence of them in a pool.
    87  //! The claim is that this history is invisible to the outcome, and the
    88  //! argument is the bracket: `check_pending` opens with `enter_scratch`, which
    89  //! resets the per-call memos and turns on an EMPTY scratch tier, and closes
    90  //! with `drop_scratch`, which resets the per-declaration caches and truncates
    91  //! the scratch tier; the persistent tier is `&PersTier`, immutable, and the
    92  //! store's own persistent tables are frozen (a persistent append is
    93  //! `M_FROZEN`'s decline); the pins are never written.  So what one record
    94  //! hands the next is CAPACITY — slot-vector lengths, `clear_fit`'s high-water
    95  //! mark, `Vec` capacities — and no lookup's answer depends on a capacity
    96  //! (`ron::hashmap2`'s refinement lemmas, `clear_fit_refines` included, are
    97  //! stated on contents).  **Why it is taken**: task #97-P5-Driver built the
    98  //! master-shaped alternative — a fresh `worker_state` per record, in the pool
    99  //! and in the verified walk alike, which makes (2) true by construction — and
   100  //! measured it on `Init` at **+16.4 % instructions** (246.7 G against
   101  //! 211.9 G, `--jobs=1`), all of it re-growing the tables every record that
   102  //! the high-water mark of task #97-P6-7 exists to keep.  (2) is a statement
   103  //! about the verified crate's `check_pending` and nothing else, so it could
   104  //! be proved; DESIGN.md's task #97-P5-Driver section says what that would
   105  //! take.

== proof/ConRon/Refine/Abs.lean#L285-L291
   285  /-- The closing call, one fixed configuration for every lemma: `ematch := 12`
   286  because the Option-monad plumbing of a leaf needs more than the default five
   287  rounds once the splits are done outside, `gen := 24` because a two-wrapper arm
   288  needs one more term generation than the default eight.  A lemma that needs
   289  more says so with the `[limit]` line in its `grind` diagnostics, and raising
   290  this default is the answer — not a per-lemma override. -/
   291  macro "rust_grind" : tactic => `(tactic| grind (ematch := 12) (gen := 24))

== proof/lakefile.toml#L24-L26
    24  [leanOptions]
    25  weak.backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency = false
    26  weak.backward.do.legacy = true

== scripts/gates.sh#L62-L100
    62  run cargo-build   env RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo build --manifest-path "$root/Cargo.toml"

    66  run provenance-self python3 "$root/scripts/provenance-selftest.py"
    67  # The other half of the same ledger: `provenance` checks what the Rust was
    68  # ported FROM (con-leche, a pinned tree), `twin-lines` what it is a port OF
    69  # (`proof/ConRon/**`, OUR tree, which every task edits — so its ranges rot
    70  # faster).  Task #97-TWIN.
    71  run twin-lines    python3 "$root/scripts/twin-lines.py" check
    72  run overview-links "$root/scripts/overview-links.sh"
    73  run holes         "$root/scripts/holes.sh" --check

    76  run gen-prelude-lean "$root/scripts/gen-prelude-lean.sh" --check
    77  # Charon + Aeneas peak at several GB each; several agents gating at once pushed
    78  # the shared 50 GB cgroup over its cap (peak 53.9 GB, 2026-09-23) and the
    79  # kernel OOM-killed aeneas (exit 137).  Serialise this one step machine-wide
    80  # through a lock in the shared `_tmp/` (every worktree sees the same one).
    81  run extract-check flock "$root/_tmp/.extract-check.lock" "$root/scripts/extract.sh" --check
    82  run lake-build    env -C "$root/proof" ${LAKE_JOBS:+LEAN_NUM_THREADS="$LAKE_JOBS"} lake build
    83  # `ConRonRefine2` is deliberately NOT a default target (a half-built P5 tier
    84  # must not block `lake build`), which means the line above never elaborates a
    85  # single module of `ConRon/Refine2/**`.  Until task #97-P5-Mut found this, a
    86  # green gate run said nothing whatsoever about a Theorem-2 lane.  It is its
    87  # own step so the OK/FAIL line names it.
    88  run lake-refine2  env -C "$root/proof" ${LAKE_JOBS:+LEAN_NUM_THREADS="$LAKE_JOBS"} lake build ConRonRefine2
    89  # **And `ConRonBridge` is not a default target either** — same hole, one tier
    90  # over, found by task #97-P3-Ind round 5 when a green gate run was followed by
    91  # a broken `lake build ConRonBridge`.  Every P3 brief has had to ask for the
    92  # target by hand for exactly this reason; now the gate does it, so a green run
    93  # means Theorem 1's spec layer elaborates too.
    94  run lake-bridge   env -C "$root/proof" ${LAKE_JOBS:+LEAN_NUM_THREADS="$LAKE_JOBS"} lake build ConRonBridge
    95  # **The composition** (task #97-COMPOSE): `ConRon/Capstone.lean`, the one
    96  # module importing both theorems, states `ConRon.Capstone.model_exists` and
    97  # `ConRon.Capstone.no_False_declaration` for the Rust pipeline.  Its own
    98  # library, not a default target, for the reason the two above are not; its
    99  # `#guard_msgs` census is what fails if a seam moves.
   100  run lake-capstone env -C "$root/proof" ${LAKE_JOBS:+LEAN_NUM_THREADS="$LAKE_JOBS"} lake build ConRonCapstone
